summary: Phase dependence of one averaged summand does not prove phase dependence of the complete averaged expression.
mechanism: 局部项与总和的无效推断

original.excerpt:
Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{s,t}
\langle\Delta_{L,s}\Theta_{M,t}\rangle
&=
\langle\overline\Delta\,\overline\Theta\rangle\\
&=
\sum_{k,j}
\left(\frac1D-p_k\right)
\left(\frac1D-r_j\right)
\mathcal B_{kj}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6.1}
$$

The phases of \(\mathcal B_{kj}\) remain. The higher terms in
`TwoLinePlaquette` similarly retain three- and four-point Bargmann data.

Thus neither the four-corner subtraction nor the full uniform average over the two cyclic shifts reduces the two-line condition to the two autocorrelation shadows.

A phase-free two-line contradiction is not obtained.
original.context: Delta and Theta are perturbations from shifting two stabilizer lines. The full TwoLinePlaquette expression contains a bilinear term and higher-order terms. The excerpt computes only the bilinear average explicitly.

witness.explanation: Phase dependence of one averaged summand does not prove phase dependence of the complete averaged expression.
witness.evidence: The source evaluates E<Delta Theta>=sum_(k,j)(1/D-p_k)(1/D-r_j) B_(kj), then says the higher terms “similarly retain” phase data without evaluating their sum. A full expression F1(theta)+F2(theta) can be phase-independent even when F1 is not (take F2=-F1+c). Therefore the displayed partial calculation does not imply the claimed noncancellation for TwoLinePlaquette. A complete average, or a coefficient that provably survives the complete sum, is required.
